speaker: Doctor
text: That absence of edema and orthopnea makes significant heart failure less likely. Have you noticed any wheezing, chest tightness, or a "smoker's cough" that worsens at night or in the morning?

text: I don't really hear any wheezing, but I do feel a tightness in my chest sometimes. The cough seems to get worse in the mornings, which is typical for my smoking history, though I've been quit for five years now.

speaker: Doctor
text: That morning worsening and chest tightness despite being a former smoker are concerning for chronic bronchitis or early COPD, but given the exertional dyspnea, we must rule out pulmonary hypertension. Have you ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure, and do you experience any palpitations or dizziness when standing up quickly?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I have been diagnosed with high blood pressure for quite some time. I don't really experience palpitations, but I do feel a bit dizzy when I stand up quickly.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with secondary Pulmonary Hypertension.
